messages.subject: MCEM error and model C++ compiling error
parts:
Hi, 

I am trying to run my model through nimble package for MCEM.
But I receive some warning messages and one error.
The warning message while compiling model are as follows:

> Cord <- compileNimble(ord)
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compiler details.
Warning: R object of different size than NimArrDouble. R obj has size 64 but NimArrDbl has size 32.
compilation finished.

> ordmcem <- ord$newModel()
setting data and initial values...
running calculate on model (any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables) ... 
checking model sizes and dimensions...

> Cordmcem <- compileNimble(ordmcem)
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compiler details.
Warning: R object of different size than NimArrDouble. R obj has size 64 but NimArrDbl has size 32.
compilation finished.

> box = list(list("tts", limits=c(0,Inf)))
> ordMCEM <- buildMCEM(model = ordmcem, latentNodes ="s",
+ boxConstraints =box)
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compiler details.
compilation finished.
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compiler details.
compilation finished.
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compiler details.
compilation finished.
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compiler details.
compilation finished.

> ordMLE <- ordMCEM$run(1000)
Error in if ((low_limits[i] > -Inf) && (hi_limits[i] < Inf)) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed.

I can't understand the meaning of these warnings and error.
I would appreciate it if you would help me to correct it.
I have attached my R code.

Best regards.
Fatemeh

messages.author: 5938cc942c6238be
messages.subject: Re: MCEM error and model C++ compiling error
parts:
Hi Fatemeh,

Thanks for emailing your errors, and for including your model along with it!  The last error message you got:

Error in if ((low_limits[i] > -Inf) && (hi_limits[i] < Inf)) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed.

is actually a bug in the way that our MCEM function dealt with multivariate nodes in models.  I've included a file called MCEM_fixed.R with a fixed version of the MCEM function.  If you load NIMBLE, and then load the functions from this MCEM_fixed.R file before running your script, the error message should no longer appear.

Also, it seems like you may want to also include the "tau1" variable in your vector of latent states for the MCEM algorithm.  This can be accomplished by setting

 latentNodes = c("s", "tau1")

in your call to buildMCEM().  Let us know if you have any other questions or run into any other issues.  Thanks again,

Nick

messages.author: 5938cc942c6238be
messages.subject: Re: MCEM error and model C++ compiling error
parts:
Hi Fatemeh,

I'm not able to reproduce the error that you got with the first model (Myoutput1.txt), but here's something that may help.  When you build a nimbleModel, you can tell NIMBLE the dimensions of the variables in the model by using the "dimensions" argument.  Most of the time, NIMBLE can figure out the dimensions of model variables itself, but for your model, the dimensions of the "b1" variable should be provided in the call to nimbleModel.  In your R script, this would look like:

ord<- nimbleModel(code = ordcode, name = "ord",
                               inits=ordInits,
                               constants = ordconst,
                               data = orddata,
                               dimensions = list(b1 = c(2, 32)))

NIMBLE has difficulty automatically detecting the dimensions of 'b1' because two different sets of dimensions are used in the model code ( "b1[1,1:m[1]]" and "b1[2,1:m[2]]"), so NIMBLE needs to be told explicitly what the correct dimensions of b1 are.  Giving these dimensions may fix the first error you got.

I also have an idea about the strange warnings you're seeing in your second set of output.  I noticed that your model has discrete valued parameters (the I1  and I2 parameters in your initial model).   The MCEM algorithm attempts to find optimal values for all of the stochastic variables in your model that aren't included in the "latentNodes" argument.  So, in your model, the MCEM algorithm is trying to optimize the I1 and I2 variables.  However, the MCEM algorithm uses an optimizer that is not designed to handle discrete parameters, so it ends up proposing non-integer values for these parameters, for example I1 = 0.5.  In turn, this is causing other model calculations to behave incorrectly, since it doesn't make sense for I1 to be anything other than 0 or 1.  To solve this, I think that you might want to include these two variables (I1 and I2) as latent variables in your MCEM algorithm - then they will no longer be optimized.

Hopefully these two suggestions will get the algorithm running for your model.  Please let me know if this doesn't work or if you encounter any other issues though! Thanks,

Nick
